The King Tide Is an Aussie-Built Camper Van That Swaps the Rear Bed for a Massive Beach Mode Lounge
23 photos
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Summit Vans Australia
Australia is one of the go-to places for van lifers due to the vast wilderness and rough but beautiful environments. There are many companies to choose from when it comes to building or buying a camper van. One of them is Summit Vans – today, I'm checking out its latest conversion.
Meet King Tide, a conversion based on a 2026 AWD Mercedes-Benz Sprinter with a 170" wheelbase, finished in Stone Grey paint. Its creator, Summit Vans, is a Wollongong, Australia-based company specializing in premium, Sprinter-based camper van conversions.
As usual, let's first take a look at the exterior. The vehicle rides on Reika wheels wrapped in BFGoodrich KO3 all-terrain tires. You can pretty much tell as soon as you lay eyes on the vehicle that it's a mobile home.
The van has a GVM suspension upgrade, with upgraded leaf springs and an upper rear shock reinforcement. This setup increases the GVM from 4,100 kg (9,039 lb.) to 4,430 kg (9,766 lb.). Summit Vans went even further and installed a Van Compass suspension kit with front and rear Falcon adjustable shocks.
At the rear, you'll come across a Weldbeat spare tire carrier/ladder combo next to another carrier holding a cargo box. Climb on the roof, and you'll discover a Wedgetail rack holding a Fiamma awning, a flat-mounted Starlink antenna, and a 200 W solar array.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Summit Vans Australia Other notable mods are Weldbeat full-length side steps, power and water hookups, and awning-style bunk windows on the sides.
Stepping inside, you'll be greeted by a bright and beautiful interior. A key detail is that it has an open layout, with no wall separating the driver's cabin from the living space.
The driver and passenger seats are mounted on factory swivel bases, so they can be turned around to face the back of the van and be used after you set up camp.
Regarding design, the customer opted for white laminated cabinetry, wood-imitating vinyl plank flooring, walls upholstered with grey woven fabric, and a bamboo slatted ceiling with recessed LED light strips. The look is complemented by a variety of black accents, such as the cabinet or drawer handles, and bamboo countertops.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Summit Vans Australia Normally, most customers opt for a seating area straight ahead of the entrance. However, this customer chose to have some extra kitchen and storage space. Specifically, they requested a counter complete with a large cabinet and a drawer. It also offers a decently sized top with additional meal prep space and charging points.
Above are two cabinets – one of them houses the rig's "command center." It includes a touchscreen display that lets you monitor and control the power system, three dimmer light switches, and various switches for the water pump, Wi-Fi, and more.
Next, we have a floor-to-ceiling unit on the same side. It integrates a microwave oven, an overhead cabinet with a plug, and a huge fridge with a freezer compartment.
The primary kitchen unit sits on the passenger side, beside the entrance. It features a deep stainless steel sink with a cover and a portable induction stove. Two overhead shelves, four drawers, a pull-out pantry, and three lower cabinets are available for storage.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Summit Vans Australia On the opposite side, Summit Vans devised one of the most sought-after camper van facilities: the bathroom. It boasts a shower with a handheld wand, an OGO Nomad toilet, and a vent that draws out the moisture outside. Moreover, you can use a wall-mounted L-Track to attach a small clothesline or other gear.
The rear part of the interior is where you'll find the van's stand-out features: Summit Vans' innovative Beach Mode rear lounge and garage configuration. You'll also notice L-Tracks on the side walls that hold two Sirocco fans, a Maxxair vent fan above, and four overhead cabinets.
Instead of a traditional fixed rear bed, the company created a massive lounge area with a Lagun table and a U-shaped couch that can be turned into a king-size bed. If for any reason you don't want to do that, you can still use the benches on the sides as two single beds.
To turn the area into a sleeping arrangement, you must remove the Lagun table and use its top, along with several extra panels, to connect the benches. Then, rearrange the cushions, and the result is an almost king-size bed. Specifically, it measures 170 centimeters (67 inches) in width and 195 centimeters (76 inches) in length.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Summit Vans Australia The benches also accommodate the utility systems. Power is on the passenger side – the electrical system's highlights are an 820 Ah battery bank and a 3,000 W inverter. You can use three charging sources to keep the batteries topped off: solar power , shore power, and DC-DC charging while the engine is running.
As for plumbing, the van is equipped with a 180-liter (47-gallon) freshwater tank inside the driver-side bench, an under-mounted 45-liter (12-gallon) greywater tank, a water filtration system, and an electric water heater.
There is one more surprise at the back of the van: an abundance of storage space. Open the rear doors, and you'll discover two surprisingly long and roomy drawers, as well as a small cabinet and a smaller drawer.
So, this Beach Mode not only cleverly uses the space for seating and sleeping, but also leaves a bunch of room for storage in the garage accessible from the back of the van.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Summit Vans Australia All in all, King Tide perfectly showcases Summit Vans' expertise in transforming vans into homes on wheels. Thanks to the Beach Mode feature, this camper van packs a flexible space without compromising adventure capability.
